HSTU already includes feature gating: jointly project inputs into U/V/Q/K, apply causal SiLU attention with relative bias, then multiply normalized aggregated values by U before output projection and residual addition. Meta’s reference implementation provides the reproducible backbone; it does not establish the proposed shifted-context input gate. [Official HSTU implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/hstu.py).

A causal extension inferred from this structure: at layer ℓ, compute c_t = h^(ℓ−1)_(t−1), then g_t = 1 + α tanh(W_c c_t + W_x h^(ℓ−1)_t + b), and feed g_t ⊙ h^(ℓ−1)_t into the HSTU block. Shift only the previous layer’s states, so all positions remain parallel and computation has no circular dependency. Initialize α=0 with ordinary nonzero projection initialization to preserve the baseline initially; zero-initialized residual scaling has precedent in [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887), although this particular gate is a proposed adaptation. For left padding, zero shifted context when the predecessor is padding, remask padded outputs, and combine causal attention with key-padding masks. At position t, predict x_(t+1) using inputs through x_t only; never condition the gate on the positive target. Read inference features at the final nonpadding position, never count−1. Validate causality by changing future tokens and confirming earlier features remain unchanged.
